tour.name: Évora & the Alentejo Private Day Trip from Lisbon: Roman Temple, Bone Chapel & Wine
tour.subtitle: A private day in the sunlit plains of the Alentejo with a licensed guide and vehicle: the walled city of Évora with its Roman temple, cathedral and Chapel of Bones, the Almendres Cromlech, older than Stonehenge, a wine estate tasting and lunch, and the cork oak landscape.

tour.overview:
East of Lisbon, the Alentejo is a land of rolling plains, cork oaks, olive groves and vineyards, with whitewashed towns on the hilltops. Its capital, Évora, has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986: a walled city with a Roman temple, a Gothic cathedral and the eerie Chapel of Bones. Nearby stands the Almendres Cromlech, one of the largest megalithic monuments in Europe.

This private day takes you there with a licensed guide and a vehicle, with a wine estate tasting and lunch.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Lisbon
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, vehicle and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• Évora: the Roman temple, the cathedral and the Chapel of Bones.
• The Almendres Cromlech.
• Cork oak forests.
• A wine estate.

WHY THIS WORKS
The cromlech and the estates are in the countryside, reachable only by car; your guide brings the layers of history together.

WHO IT SUITS
History lovers, wine lovers, couples and families.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For the coast, choose our Sintra and Cascais day trip.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The Alentejo is very hot in summer. The drive from Lisbon is about 1 hour 30 minutes.

days.name: Évora, the Chapel of Bones, the Almendres Cromlech and a wine estate
days.description:
What to expect: the Roman, medieval and prehistoric Alentejo, with a licensed guide, private vehicle, entrances, tasting and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 8:30 and cross the Tagus on the 25 de Abril bridge, driving east through cork oak country. You stop to see how cork is harvested from the trees by hand every nine years.

In Évora, you see the Roman Temple, its granite columns with marble capitals standing in the main square since the 1st century, and the cathedral, whose cloister and rooftop give views over the plains. In the Church of São Francisco, you enter the Chapel of Bones, its walls lined with the bones and skulls of some 5,000 people, with an inscription that reads 'We bones that are here, for yours we wait'. You walk through the whitewashed lanes and the Praça do Giraldo.

Lunch is at a wine estate, with Alentejo dishes such as black pork and bread soups, and a tasting of the region's rich reds and whites. In the afternoon, you visit the Almendres Cromlech, a circle of nearly a hundred standing stones among cork oaks, raised from about 6000 BC, before driving back to Lisbon.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Pick-up in Lisbon.
09:30 – Cork oak stop.
10:15 – Évora: the Roman temple and cathedral.
11:30 – Chapel of Bones.
12:15 – Walk through the town.
13:15 – Lunch and tasting at a wine estate.
15:30 – Almendres Cromlech.
17:30 – Back in Lisbon.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The hilltop village of Monsaraz can be added on a longer day.
• An olive oil tasting can be arranged.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, licensed guide, entrances, wine tasting, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: extra wine, tips.

Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Are entrances included?
faq.answer: Yes: the cathedral and the Chapel of Bones.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, at a wine estate with a tasting.

faq.question: Is the Chapel of Bones suitable for children?
faq.answer: Most children find it fascinating rather than frightening; your guide explains it gently.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. The town is fairly flat; the cathedral roof has stairs.

faq.question: Can non-drinkers join?
faq.answer: Of course; the lunch is excellent and juices are available.

faq.question: How hot is it?
faq.answer: Over 35°C in summer; we adapt the timing.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light clothes, a hat, sun protection and comfortable shoes.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: March to June and September to November.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not obligatory in Portugal, but rounding up or leaving 5 to 10 percent for a guide or driver you were happy with is appreciated.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
